public.prompt: A documentation reader contains hundreds of off-screen sections with uneven heights. `content-visibility: auto` cuts initial rendering work, but the scrollbar thumb and scroll position shift before sections are visited. After a section is rendered once, future skips should reuse its measured size. Which sizing contract fits?

options.label: Pair `content-visibility: auto` with `contain-intrinsic-size: auto <estimate>` tuned from representative sections.
Pair `content-visibility: hidden` with fixed heights on each section and reveal only the active heading.
Pair `content-visibility: auto` with `overflow: hidden` and measure every section height during startup.

optionRationales.explanation: The estimate supplies layout space before rendering, and the `auto` form lets a later off-screen skip use the section's remembered size.
Hidden content remains skipped regardless of viewport relevance, while fixed heights cannot model the stated uneven sections accurately.
optionRationales.plausibility: Explicit heights reserve deterministic scroll space and hidden content avoids rendering work.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: Full sections must become available as users scroll and their heights vary.

optionRationales.explanation: Measuring every section up front defeats the deferred rendering budget, and overflow clipping does not provide remembered intrinsic sizing.
optionRationales.plausibility: Known section heights would make the scrollbar stable before the user begins scrolling.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: Initial work must remain bounded instead of rendering or measuring the full document.

answerProof.summary: The intrinsic-size placeholder reserves approximate space while off-screen content is skipped. With the `auto` form, the browser can replace that estimate with the last rendered size when the same section becomes off-screen again.
decisiveConstraints: Unvisited sections need an estimated layout contribution.
Previously rendered sections should reuse their measured size.

claims.statement: `content-visibility: auto` can skip rendering work for content that is not relevant to the user while preserving the element in document features.
The `auto <length>` intrinsic-size form uses a placeholder before rendering and can use the element's last remembered size after actual size information exists.
